newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan brass mills cut 1996/97 demand forecast.
newsitem.headline: Japan brass mills cut 1996/97 demand forecast.

text.p: The Japan Brass Makers' Association said on Friday it had cut its forecast of demand for brass mill products in the year to next March to 1.170 million tonnes from its March forecast of 1.188 million tonnes.
The revision represents a 2.8 percent decline from the year before, versus the estimate in March of a 1.3 percent decline.
Japanese domestic demand for 1996/97 is estimated at 969,830 tonnes, off 2.8 percent from the year before, while exports are expected to fall 2.5 percent to 200,170 tonnes.
Among major products, forecast demand for copper sheet was lowered to 239,300 tonnes, off 4.3 percent from the previous year, reflecting sluggish demand from the chip sector.
The copper tubing forecast was raised to 254,570 tonnes, reflecting good demand from carmakers but still 1.7 percent below last year's level.

Record sales of air conditioners this year have also buoyed demand. But association officials said air conditioner sales were expected to dip next year to about 7.6 million units from this year's 7.8 million. Inventories were expected to reach two million units, which they said would be excessive.
Brass rod demand this year was estimated at 313,820, below the March estimate and off 0.8 percent from last year's level.
